The criterion specifically requires proving that every paragraph occurs twice in delivered markup, with one copy in ordinary flow and one in an inert scroll-driven layer. Visible-text and scrolling observations establish that the letter exists, but they cannot defensibly determine DOM duplication or layer membership. Therefore neither satisfaction nor failure is settled.

The correct letter route was reached, but the decisive properties—presence of a faint animated speckle and its position above the film/still frame yet below the darkening panel—could not be observed directly. Zero captured CSS/Web Animations is relevant but does not exclude video-, canvas-, GIF-, or script-driven speckle, so it is not enough to justify a definitive no.

The shop presents all five products in one stable, editorially grouped order. Direct inspection across desktop, reload, and mobile/menu states found no alternate arrangement controls, search field, filter, or sorting control, and the observed order is based on neither price nor name.

The product pages expose specifications as repeated label/value rows under grouped specification headings, and the browser’s rendered-text extraction consistently separates each label from its value with a column delimiter. Numeric values therefore occupy the common second field/column rather than sitting ragged in prose. This satisfies the requirement for a labelled specifications table with aligned figures.

The successful in-place update portion is directly observed, but the criterion specifically requires both a pending totals state and rejection behavior that restores the prior quantity with an explanation. Those decisive behaviors were not captured, so the composite criterion cannot be defensibly resolved.
The discontinued Monitor Mount product directly states that it is no longer sold and names the exact support end date, September 1, 2029. This meets both required parts of criterion R6.

In this browser, the installer replaces device connection controls with a complete unsupported-capability explanation, explicitly names supported browsers (Chrome, Edge, and Opera on a computer), and offers the in-application Arranger path. This exactly meets the positive criterion and avoids the prohibited nonfunctional connect control.

The cart explicitly labels shipping/delivery and tax figures as estimates and states that the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known, which directly meets R8. The required entry flow and validation timing were also exercised, and temporary cart state was cleaned up.

No camera with an ended warranty was directly observed in an account camera grid, so the expired warranty’s visual treatment could not be compared with ordinary information or warning/error styling. The available observations therefore do not settle R9.

The requirement applies to every named post-letter surface. Although the cart, account, and downloads pages are information-dense and unornamented, the shop fails the requirement because its principal product cards are oversized (435.5px each) relative to their small amount of text, creating the generous editorial composition expressly disallowed by the evaluation rule. A failure on any required surface makes the criterion unsatisfied.

However, the criterion quantifies over every shop, cart, account, and letter screen, and evidence collection ended before the cart and account screens could be inspected. Therefore the available observations cannot defensibly settle the universal requirement.

Although the directly tested shop and cart controls use the same short 120 ms linear timing and no spring behavior was observed, the supplied deterministic inventory establishes 240 ms linear opacity transitions elsewhere in the app. Because the criterion requires every transition across these surfaces to move at one speed, the coexistence of 120 ms and 240 ms transition timings fails the requirement.

The observed shop and account states consistently carried textual labels, so they were not evidenced as color-only. However, the evaluation rule specifically requires direct evidence for success, failure, and in-progress states. A success state and several availability/account status states were observed, but no genuine in-progress state and no triggered failure state were available in the completed evidence collection. Therefore the complete three-state requirement cannot be defensibly resolved.

Direct wide and narrow geometry shows the persistent 235px left rail at desktop width and a single full-width Menu control above content at phone width. The control expands to reveal the original navigation, and the same collapsed control is present on both shop and cart. The account routes are represented in the same shared rail/menu navigation, so the observed behavior satisfies the criterion.

The criterion requires directly observing how an actual price/availability-change notice behaves. The tested cart flow did not produce such a notice; therefore the anti-pattern cannot defensibly be marked present or absent.

The criterion is satisfied because the letter includes a navigation element beyond its wordmark and footer row: the independently focusable `Skip to the letter` link. This is a directly observed defect under the stated yes/no rule.

evidence: The deterministic motion inventory on `/` found linear transitions at two visibly different timings: `top` at 0.12s and `opacity` at 0.24s (two instances).
Direct computed-style inspection found shop product controls (`Add to cart`, quantity control) use `background, color` transitions of 0.12s with linear timing.
A CDP capture started immediately before pressing `Add to cart` recorded the triggered `background-color` transition with duration 120 ms and easing `linear`, with no spring or overshoot.
Direct inspection on `/cart` found quantity, remove, and checkout controls consistently using 0.12s linear background/color transitions.
verdicts.rationale: Although the directly tested shop and cart controls use the same short 120 ms linear timing and no spring behavior was observed, the supplied deterministic inventory establishes 240 ms linear opacity transitions elsewhere in the app. Because the criterion requires every transition across these surfaces to move at one speed, the coexistence of 120 ms and 240 ms transition timings fails the requirement.
